articles.title: Recursive Governance: When Agents Write the Rules They Execute
articles.excerpt: We almost lost forty modules to a file that never changed. The sync job ran every six hours, mirroring our shared working directory into a test workspace. At 21:47 on a Tuesday, it removed about forty…
articles.body: We almost lost forty modules to a file that never changed. The sync job ran every six hours, mirroring our shared working directory into a test workspace. At 21:47 on a Tuesday, it removed about forty private modules that should have been ignored. The filter file was missing one pattern. That's it. One pattern. A colleague had restructured the source tree three days earlier, added a directory, and didn't update the filter file. The script didn't warn, didn't ask, didn't fail. It just mirrored the state it was told to mirror. Restoring the modules took us almost two hours, one by one from the backup box. The filter file was a static text file. It encoded what the sync could delete and what it couldn't, and it had no idea that the real inventory had changed.
articles.author: Open Human

articles.body: A process historian stores time-series data from PLCs, SCADA and sensors, often for years, and serves it back quickly for trends, reports and analytics. Most selection mistakes come from comparing feature lists instead of checking fit with what you already run. Start from your SCADA or connectivity layer and your analytics layer, then pick the historian that connects cleanly to both. Purpose-built process historians Built for industrial tags, compression and long retention. AVEVA PI System (AVEVA, formerly OSIsoft PI): enterprise operational data infrastructure. Proficy Historian (GE Vernova): part of the Proficy suite, archiving process data at site and enterprise level.

articles.body: Color contrast is the number one accessibility failure on the web. According to WebAIM's Million analysis, 83.6% of all websites fail WCAG contrast requirements on at least one element. Adding a dark mode toggle to your site doesn't fix that statistic — for most teams, it creates an entirely new set of contrast failures that no one checked because the light mode tested fine. Test individual color pairs with the color contrast checker ; for code-level fixes in React apps, see the React accessibility checker . The ada compliance color checker problem in 2026 is this: most teams test contrast for one theme. They pick colors for light mode, run them through a contrast ratio tool, confirm they pass 4.5:1, and ship.

articles.title: Presence Membership Semantics — What Realtime Signals Cannot Tell Dispatch Polls
articles.excerpt: Treat realtime presence membership as a recent observation, never as proof that a participant saw, processed, or answered a live poll. Explained in operational terms, presence can tell you which ident…
articles.body: Treat realtime presence membership as a recent observation, never as proof that a participant saw, processed, or answered a live poll. Explained in operational terms, presence can tell you which identities have represented connections; it cannot tell you who received the question. For a logistics session, keep poll delivery and vote acceptance in a durable event path, attach explicit identifiers, and use presence only to improve the interface. TL;DR: a driver appearing in a session roster means the presence system currently associates that identity with one or more live connections. It cannot establish that the poll reached the driver's screen, that the screen was visible, that the driver was able to respond, or that a missing connection represents an absent person.

articles.body: Short answer: Don't keep the request open, and don't put the clock inside the web server. For one bounded daily cleanup report, let cron launch a separate Node.js command that claims the business date, performs the cleanup, sends the report, and exits; add a durable queue only when independent retries or parallel delivery justify the extra running system. That answer starts with isolation, not fashion. A developer-tools control plane might delete expired preview environments at 02:00 UTC and mail a report afterward. The API request that configured the policy has finished long before then.

articles.title: The moon is shrinking. 10,000 cracks on the lunar surface reveal by how much
articles.excerpt: One new study shows how much the moon has diminished over time.
articles.body: The moon is shrinking, and scientists are narrowing in on exactly how much our natural satellite has dwindled over the years. The moon is thought to have formed from a violent collision between a massive object and our young Earth roughly 4.5 billion years ago, and its interior is still gradually cooling off from this ancient collision. As it cools, the moon contracts, leading to a long, slow shrinking process . Now, in a new study, scientists think that they have figured out how much smaller the moon is actually getting. In this new study, scientists analyzing images snapped by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) have spotted over 10,000 young faults, or cracks across the moon's surface.

articles.body: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Research teams at NASA’s Glenn Research Center are involved in developing theory and software to predict the noise from aircraft engines. This software helps engineers to design and analyze new and improved aircraft propulsion systems. Copies of our software can be requested from NASA’s Software Catalog. Aerodynamic predictions of a the hot exhaust flow through a dual stream nozzle with chevrons. NASA JeNo Development of jet noise prediction codes is multifaceted. Since JeNo predicts jet noise using Lilley’s Acoustic Analogy and the mean flow solutions from a Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) code, accurate acoustic predictions hinge on accurate aerodynamic predictions.

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of the unethical and likely illegal acts its agents are performing. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
